answer: In an agent economy, every identity must lock a bond into a shared vault before it can bid on tasks. A sybil attacker who spawns a thousand fake agents therefore pays a thousand deposits, and each deposit is the ridge that separates honest participants from cheap fakes: crossing it costs real capital, not a new email. Validators periodically audit behavior, and any agent caught colluding has its vault stake slashed, so losing capital compounds with every clone. Attackers cannot harbor unpunished duplicates because the cost scales linearly with identities while honest agents pay only once.
